output.title: The Person in Front of You
output.excerpt: Most of the harm people do to one another is done by people who believe, in the moment, that they are justified. Not by the rare monster who enjoys suffering. By the parent who is tired. The official who is owed a favor. The neighbor who heard a story. The driver who is late. The crowd that would…

summary:
The essay is in `./output/essay.md`. It is called "The Person in Front of You."

It treats one shared reading as common knowledge: a few duties we can expect of each other. Treat the person in front of you as real. Pause before harm or rumor. Repair what you broke, without trapping anyone in abuse. Raise children with safety, language, and no hitting. Tell the truth people will rely on, and disagree without unmaking each other. Do the easy rescue, including fluid replacement for diarrhea, pressure on bleeding, handwashing, breastfeeding, vaccines, and not being the disaster yourself. Do the work honestly, especially toward people who cannot punish you. The closing lines are meant to be said out loud.
